digest.component_or_area: enrich gate marker (write-path drain O(1) optimization)
propositions: The enrich gate marker is binary: a single pending entry disables the O(1) fast path store-wide, forcing O(store) full walks on every subsequent write until the pending set empties.
Measured cost scales linearly with store size and is only weakly sensitive to backlog depth; at 4,938 tickets one pending entry costs ~1.2s per write versus ~0.11ms with zero pending.
The marker should generalize from all-or-nothing (whole store quiet) to set-valued form (quiet outside a recorded live set), scoping walks to O(backlog) reductions instead of O(store).
Scoped probes must not rewrite the marker so TTL remains bounded by the last full walk; full scans always write the marker including the live set.
The marker must only ever assert absence of pending work; pending verdicts always come from reducing real queue events; a stale marker can defer a drain (TTL-bounded) but never manufacture work.

Service order parity must hold: the extracted per-entry scan loop (including f400 sort on (not_before_ns, id)) is shared by full and scoped paths, returning identical ordering for the same store state.
